name: Emon Roy Bappy
headline: Research and Development Engineer
summary:
Currently, I am a Research and Development Engineer at Cybernetics Hi-Tech Solutions (Pvt.) Ltd. where I am focused on the development and analysis of military robots for Bangladesh Army. Our team has already delivered two Explosive Ordinance Disposal Remotely Operated Vehicles (EOD-ROVs), which have been deployed in United Nations Peacekeeping Missions. Currently, I am working on a Man-Portable EOD ROV project along with my teammates. My key responsibilities include Design for Manufacturing and Assembly (DfMA), stress analysis, structural topology optimization, additive manufacturing methods for prototyping like Fused Deposition Modeling (FDM), molding of soft materials like silicone, subtractive manufacturing like CNC milling and Electro Discharge Machining (EDM). Recently, we have started working on composite materials. For the first time in Bangladesh’s history, we successfully implemented the resin infusion method to manufacture structural components using carbon fiber, achieving an industrial-grade solution within our own composite fabrication lab. This milestone not only demonstrates our manufacturing capabilities and knowledge but also creates a precedent for the country’s manufacturing infrastructure. 
 During my undergraduate studies in Mechanical Engineering at Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology (BUET), I built a strong foundation in electromechanical systems, computer-aided design, PCB design, and finite element analysis, which naturally pushed me to explore the intersection of robotics and manufacturing. As a third-year student in the mechanical department, I collaborated with my team to develop a bio-inspired soft robotic fish and a mechanical solution for variable capacity cooling tower. During my undergraduate thesis, I designed and fabricated a soft robotic actuator to replace the conventional rigid actuator in the medical robots used for Minimally Invasive Surgery (MIS). The soft actuator has three degrees of freedom to reach any area at the time of surgery, minimizing the number of incisions and reducing patient’s recovery time. 
 My goal is to pursue cutting-edge research that bridges the robotics field and manufacturing methods, ultimately contributing to the development of resilient and intelligent manufacturing solutions for humanitarian applications.

projects.subtitle: An Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD) Remotely Operated Vehicle (ROV) Designed to Be Carried and Deployed by a Soldier

projects.longDescription:
Currently, we are developing a man-transportable EOD ROV, building on our experience with the previously developed medium-platform EOD ROV, Jontro Soinik v1.0. We began by analyzing the limitations of the earlier robot and identifying new challenges associated with designing a smaller platform. In the next phase, our focus was on constructing a lightweight structure that maximizes strength, maintains a low center of gravity, and introduces a new degree of freedom in the arm through a screw-based telescopic beam. To further reduce weight and enhance mechanical performance, we are integrating carbon fiber components into the robot. These parts are fabricated in-house using resin infusion, compression molding, and hand layup techniques within our composite fabrication laboratory.
The Man-Transportable EOD ROV is a compact bomb disposal robot built for high-stakes counter-IED operations. It navigates complex terrain with ease, using a dual-mode drive system and adaptive flipper mechanisms. The detachable manipulator arm offers precise control and tool-mounting flexibility, making it ideal for handling hazardous materials. Operators benefit from real-time situational awareness through a multi-camera setup, including a PTZ unit and wrist-mounted views. The robot’s control unit features a daylight-readable display and supports both wired and wireless communication for uninterrupted mission execution. Its rugged build and shock-absorbing design ensure durability in harsh environments. Integrated overload protection and intelligent motion control enhance operational safety and reliability. Designed for tactical deployment, the Man-Transportable EOD ROV combines mobility, modularity, and mission-ready resilience in a compact form.

projects.subtitle: A Medium Platfom EOD ROV (Updated Version of Smart Soinik 1.0)
projects.description: Jontro Soinik 1.0 (JS1.0) is Bangladesh’s third generation and most advanced indigenously developed Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD) Remotely Operated Vehicle (ROV) with environmental adaptability and disrupter firing capacity, which is first of its kind, engineered for ...
projects.longDescription:
Jontro Soinik 1.0 (JS1.0) is Bangladesh’s third generation and most advanced indigenously developed Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD) Remotely Operated Vehicle (ROV) with environmental adaptability and disrupter firing capacity, which is first of its kind, engineered for rapid deployment and rugged performance in high-risk environments. Successfully tested by the Bangladesh Army, including live disrupter firing and IP55 water protection trials, it proves its readiness for real-world missions. Equipped with advanced electronics like GPS, thermal imaging, IR night vision, 4x optical zoom, and a 2MP camera system, it supports precision surveillance and remote neutralization of threats. With robust mechanical capabilities—stair climbing, slope handling (up to 40°), 360° claw rotation, 40kg grip force, and a lifting capacity of up to 20kg—the ROV is built for maneuverability and strength. Its 16Ah battery enables extended operations with active/passive overload protection, self-diagnostics, and fast recharging. Designed for battlefield reliability, Jontro Soinik 1.0 embodies innovation, adaptability, and national pride in defense technology. 
 Jontro Soinik 1.0 is set for deployment in 2025 under the UN Peacekeeping Mission in the Republic of the Congo.

projects.longDescription: Smart Soinik 1.0 (SS1.0) is the second-generation, indigenously developed Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD) Remotely Operated Vehicle (ROV) from Bangladesh, designed for rapid deployment and unmatched performance in high-risk operational environments. Rigorously tested and validated by the Bangladesh Army, SS1.0 combines cutting-edge electronics — such as thermal imaging, IR night vision, 4× optical zoom, and high-resolution video capture — with rugged mechanical strength, including stair-climbing ability, 30° slope handling, 360° claw rotation, and a powerful 40 kg grip force. Powered by a 16 Ah battery system with overload protection, self-diagnostics, and fast recharge capability, it ensures extended field endurance and operational reliability. On May 5, 2024, Smart Soinik 1.0 was officially gifted to the Peruvian Armed Forces by the Bangladesh Army and is now proudly deployed under the United Nations Peacekeeping Mission in the Republic of Mali, showcasing Bangladesh's growing footprint in global defense innovation and humanitarian operations.

projects.title: Hilsha-Bot
projects.subtitle: A Bio-Inspired Soft Robotic Fish
projects.description: This bio-inspired soft robotic fish intended for concealment during tasks like underwater wildlife monitoring or reconnaissance. Its construction utilizes a soft silicone material covering a continuum structure, essential for replicating the natural, flexible undulatory ...
projects.longDescription: This bio-inspired soft robotic fish intended for concealment during tasks like underwater wildlife monitoring or reconnaissance. Its construction utilizes a soft silicone material covering a continuum structure, essential for replicating the natural, flexible undulatory movement of aquatic species. Propulsion is achieved using a soft tail actuator that executes a fish-like undulating motion, classified specifically as carangiform swimming. This natural method of locomotion is crucial because it allows the robot to integrate into the aquatic environment without disturbing other underwater entities. The tail movement is driven by a curved single-shaft mechanism which reciprocates the tail's sheets left and right to generate the required thrust. Depth control is managed by an innovative buoyancy control unit housed within the body. This unit operates through a piston-cylinder mechanism that creates a vacuum to adjust the overall specific weight of the robot. This vacuum piston-based approach offers the significant benefit of a longer operational period compared to traditional systems constrained by gas depletion. The robot is equipped with artificial pectoral and dorsal fins that collaboratively manage movement direction and stability. The pectoral fins control steering by generating lift forces, while the dorsal fin enhances overall stability, and an enclosure protects the sensitive electronics housed in the head section

projects.title: Soft Robotic Actuator
projects.subtitle: A Tendon-Driven Soft Actuator for Surgical Operation
projects.description: The soft actuator is a tendon-driven soft continuum robot designed for minimally invasive surgery. It is fabricated primarily from inert and biocompatible silicone rubber, utilizing a process that includes Fused Deposition Modelling for creating molds and subsequent liquid silicone rubber...
projects.longDescription: The soft actuator is a tendon-driven soft continuum robot designed for minimally invasive surgery. It is fabricated primarily from inert and biocompatible silicone rubber, utilizing a process that includes Fused Deposition Modelling for creating molds and subsequent liquid silicone rubber moulding. The actuator achieves a minimum of three degrees of freedom, including bending along two axes and rotation around its central axis. The structure is based on repeating single units, with a typical diameter of 15 mm. These units are assembled by routing tension cables, which can be made of material like unfilled Nylon 6.6, through their multiple circular channels. The system operates by applying tension to these cables to induce bending or rotation.The finalized design (Version 2.1) features separate units dedicated to bending and rotation functionalities, enhancing efficiency, and includes an additional internal hole to accommodate a tool grabbing mechanism and power cable routing. A thin rigid layer is used between adjacent units to help minimize frictional loss. Control is managed through a sophisticated closed-loop system incorporating four DC motors connected to the tendons, an Arduino development board, and a custom PCB, using motor current as real-time feedback. Finite element analysis was utilized during development to predict the structure’s deformation and stress behavior under load

projects.title: Titan, A Large Scale FDM Printer
projects.subtitle: A FDM 3D Printer with a Bed Volume of 510mm×510mm×550mm
projects.description: Titan is a large-format FDM printer designed for high-speed, precision additive manufacturing with a 510 × 510 × 550 mm build volume, ±0.1 mm accuracy, and 0.02 mm repeatability; it features CoreXY motion with GT2 belts, a direct-drive dual-gear extruder (MK8), a 0.8 mm swappable nozzle, and a heated...
projects.longDescription: Titan is a large-format FDM printer designed for high-speed, precision additive manufacturing with a 510 × 510 × 550 mm build volume, ±0.1 mm accuracy, and 0.02 mm repeatability; it features CoreXY motion with GT2 belts, a direct-drive dual-gear extruder (MK8), a 0.8 mm swappable nozzle, and a heated glass bed up to 120°C. The hotend reaches 300°C for engineering-grade thermoplastics, powered by a Bigtreetech controller with TMC2209 drivers running Marlin 2.0 firmware. Titan includes a 4.3 inch touchscreen with jog wheel, Wi-Fi, Ethernet, and USB-C connectivity. Safety features comprise thermal-runaway protection, power-loss resume, and door interlock. The MeanWell 24V / 30A PFC power supply ensures stable operation. Titan supports rapid prototyping and functional part fabrication with silent actuation and high-flow extrusion. Its optimized motion system enables smooth, vibration-free performance. The printer achieves up to 200 mm/s print speed, with a recommended range of 60–120 mm/s. Layer resolution spans 50–400 µm for fine detail and robust builds. Titan is ideal for research, industrial prototyping, and large-scale fabrication workflows.

projects.title: Fixed Wing VTOL UAV
projects.subtitle: A Handmade Prototype Of Fixed Wing Unmanned Aerial Vehicle
projects.description: This project involves the development, construction, and outdoor manual testing of a small-scale fixed-wing VTOL UAV prototype featuring a 2-meter rectangular wingspan, brushless motor-driven propulsion, and four aerodynamic control surfaces (two wing ailerons and two V-tail ruddervators). The UAV structure...
projects.longDescription: This project involves the development, construction, and outdoor manual testing of a small-scale fixed-wing VTOL UAV prototype featuring a 2-meter rectangular wingspan, brushless motor-driven propulsion, and four aerodynamic control surfaces (two wing ailerons and two V-tail ruddervators). The UAV structure employs polystyrene foam for core bulk, 3D-printed PLA and laser cut PVC sheet for precision parts and skeleton, and polyurethane foam for added resilience, balancing low-weight and manufacturability with sufficient mechanical strength and crash tolerance. The prototype serves as a dedicated empirical platform to analyze aerodynamic stability, control response, and transition dynamics between VTOL and fixed-wing flight regimes, all critical precursors to heavy-payload UAV validation. Aerodynamically, the project emphasizes the hazardous yet essential transition corridor, where careful control allocation and mixing strategies across the wing and V-tail surfaces mitigate the risks of stall, loss of control, or structural overload. Brushless motor sizing and integration is optimized for rapid thrust response and efficient power consumption, with cooling and reliability characterized empirically to support scaling toward higher-power, payload-carrying platforms. Structural design studies focus on low-density, foam-based airframes with PLA and PVC reinforcement, utilizing iterative flight testing and post-flight inspection to validate modeling and optimize joint assemblies and impact resistance. The experimental flight program applies standardized pre-flight checks and manual piloting to instrumented free-flight testing, allowing direct measurement of handling qualities, stability margins, and failure behaviors in a real-world context. Rich data acquisition and telemetry systems—integrating IMUs, GPS, servo feedback, and power sensors—enable high-resolution analysis of aerodynamic coefficients, control effectiveness, and transition behavior, with all results feeding into multi-criteria performance evaluation, model validation, and future controller/autopilot development. The project's outcomes provide critical empirical data and validated methodologies that directly inform scaling for a 50 kg-payload VTOL UAV, establishing confidence in the aerodynamic design, control strategy, and structural philosophy underpinning robust, certifiable heavy-lift UAV platforms. Overall, this prototype serves as a pivotal technological bridge, accelerating the transition from experimental concept to operational, heavy-payload-capable VTOL UAVs in a scalable, cost-effective, and risk-limited manner.

projects.title: Mars Rover- Anweshan, Renaissance
projects.subtitle: A Rover for University Mars Rover Competition
projects.description: This ROV is a multifunctional Mars rover developed for the Rover Challenges, designed to perform autonomous navigation, scientific exploration, and precision manipulation tasks on simulated Martian terrain...
projects.longDescription:
This ROV is a multifunctional Mars rover developed for the Rover Challenges, designed to perform autonomous navigation, scientific exploration, and precision manipulation tasks on simulated Martian terrain. Mechanically, it features a four-wheel rocker suspension system with large-diameter aluminum wheels and grousers for enhanced traction on rocky and sandy surfaces. The chassis provides ample internal space for housing scientific tools and electronics, while a 6-DOF robotic arm with a two-claw gripper enables tasks such as probe placement, sample collection, and switch manipulation. The arm’s joints are powered by a combination of stepper motors, geared DC motors, and high-torque servos, allowing for fine control and adaptability across maintenance and probing tasks.
Electrically, the rover integrates two compute units—Raspberry Pi 4B for teleoperation and Jetson Xavier NX for autonomous functions like navigation and image processing. STM32 microcontrollers interface with motor drivers, encoders, and sensors, enabling real-time control and feedback. The power distribution system includes four Li-Po batteries, buck converters, and safety features such as fuses and emergency stop buttons. Perception is achieved through a RealSense D435i stereo camera, multiple Raspberry Pi cameras, and a BNO055 IMU for localization and mapping. Communication between the rover and base station is maintained via Ubiquiti Rocket M5 modules over a ROS network. The software stack includes RTAB-Map for SLAM, MoveIt for motion planning, and custom Python interfaces for operator control, ensuring robust performance across all mission phases.

projects.title: Formula Student Vehicle
projects.subtitle: A Combustion Vehicle for Formula Student Competition
projects.description: This project centers on the design and development of a student-built Formula Student race car, engineered for performance, reliability, and manufacturability. A steel tube space frame chassis was chosen to meet weight and strength requirements, with iterative analysis...
projects.longDescription:
This project centers on the design and development of a student-built Formula Student race car, engineered for performance, reliability, and manufacturability. A steel tube space frame chassis was chosen to meet weight and strength requirements, with iterative analysis optimizing torsional rigidity and impact resistance. The suspension system employs unequal-length double wishbones with push-rod actuation, ensuring minimal camber gain and stable roll center behavior during cornering, bump, and rebound. Steering geometry is based on Ackermann principles to prevent outer wheel skidding, and the braking system uses CNC-machined aluminum calipers with locally fabricated discs for effective heat dissipation and structural integrity. Aerodynamic components such as undertray, diffuser, and sidepods were designed to enhance downforce and cooling efficiency while minimizing drag and manufacturing complexity.
The powertrain system features a KTM Duke 390 engine, selected for its lightweight, liquid-cooled configuration and compatibility with event regulations. The intake system includes a 20mm restrictor optimized to reduce flow separation, while the exhaust length and diameter were calculated using Smith and Bell equations to match target RPM ranges. The fuel tank, fabricated from AISI 1100 aluminum alloy, is positioned behind the driver for optimal packaging. The differential bracket, CNC-machined from aluminum, ensures precise alignment and structural integrity under chain tension. Throughout the project, simulation tools like SolidWorks, Ansys, and CFD analysis were used to validate mechanical, thermal, and fluid performance, ensuring that each subsystem meets the demands of competitive motorsport.

projects.title: IPAS- Nirveek v1.0
projects.subtitle: Design Concept for a Drone in the Martian Environment
projects.description: This project presents the development of Nirveek V1.0, an autonomous UAV designed for Martian exploration under the International Planetary Aerial Systems 2021. Engineered to navigate harsh Martian terrain, Nirveek features a lightweight...
projects.longDescription: This project presents the development of Nirveek V1.0, an autonomous UAV designed for Martian exploration under the International Planetary Aerial Systems 2021. Engineered to navigate harsh Martian terrain, Nirveek features a lightweight quadcopter frame (128×128×35 cm, 5.1 kg) capable of sustained 10-minute flights at altitudes up to 45 meters. It integrates a 360° vision system powered by a customized GoPro Max and Lidar, and relies on visual-inertial odometry (VIO) for GPS-independent navigation. Built on ROS for mission planning, the UAV includes a modular design for ease of repair, a 10000mAh LiPo battery, and a thermal management system to maintain operability in extreme temperatures. A custom gas compression system enables accurate sensor readings by heating and pressurizing Martian air, while a 2.4GHz radio link ensures communication up to 6.5 km. Designed with serviceability and adaptability in mind, Nirveek is equipped to perform autonomous missions, detect environmental hazards, and support future planetary research.

projects.title: Cooling Tower
projects.subtitle: Miniature Prototype of a Mechanically Driven Variable-Flow Nozzle Integrated Cooling Tower
projects.description: This project focuses on the design, fabrication, and performance evaluation of a cooling tower equipped with a variable nozzle mechanism to adapt to changing operational demands. The system integrates a feedback control strategy to regulate water...
projects.longDescription: This project focuses on the design, fabrication, and performance evaluation of a cooling tower equipped with a variable nozzle mechanism to adapt to changing operational demands. The system integrates a feedback control strategy to regulate water flow and airflow, with a key innovation in dynamically adjusting the number of active nozzles based on flow rate. Three nozzle configurations were explored—double pipe, double disk, and double sheet mechanisms—with the double sheet design selected for its superior manufacturability and surface finish. The cooling tower body is constructed from 5 mm acrylic sheets, reinforced with wood to support the belt pulley system, while plastic film fills are used to maximize heat transfer efficiency. This modular and responsive design aims to improve cooling performance, reduce energy consumption, and offer scalable solutions for industrial applications.

projects.title: Aqua Monitor
projects.subtitle: A Digital Water Quality & Flow Monitoring Device with a Proper Billing System
projects.description: This project introduces a smart water monitoring system composed of two integrated units: one for assessing water quality and another for tracking water usage. The water quality monitoring unit features a cylindrical flow-through design to minimize...
projects.longDescription: This project introduces a smart water monitoring system composed of two integrated units: one for assessing water quality and another for tracking water usage. The water quality monitoring unit features a cylindrical flow-through design to minimize impedance and houses four key sensors—TDS, pH, turbidity, and dissolved oxygen—managed by an ESP32 microcontroller with built-in Wi-Fi and Bluetooth for seamless data transmission. A UV light module is incorporated to neutralize microbial contaminants, ensuring safe drinking water. The water usage monitoring unit includes a flow sensor to measure consumption and an automated solenoid valve that can shut off supply in response to anomalies. Together, these modules enable both users and service providers to monitor real-time water metrics, promoting transparency and accountability. The circuit powering this system includes essential features such as ESD protection, a manual reset via push-button switch, USB debugging support, dual power compatibility (12V adapter or rechargeable battery), a built-in display for live data visualization, and an LED indicator for system status. By digitizing water quality and usage data, the system supports fair billing practices—addressing the current issue of uniform charges despite varying consumption—and enables personalized access through customer ID via web and mobile platforms. Targeting over 15 million WASA users, this solution not only enhances public health and resource management but also lays the foundation for scalable, economic water treatment and equitable service delivery.

projects.longDescription: This project involves the design and development of an autonomous ground robot capable of line-based navigation and obstacle avoidance, using IR sensors for path detection and a sonar sensor for real-time environmental awareness. Built with a combination of plastic wood and nylon for structural durability, the robot is powered by an Arduino Nano and driven by an L298n motor driver. A PID control algorithm was implemented to enhance line-tracking precision, and after extensive tuning, the proportional and derivative gains were optimized for stable performance. The robot successfully solved complex line mazes and was able to identify the shortest path after completing a full scan of the environment. Key responsibilities included schematic and PCB design, breadboard prototyping, programming and debugging, component soldering and final assembly, followed by test runs using Altium, EasyEDA, and Arduino IDE.

projects.longDescription: This ergonomic height-adjustable table is designed to support a wide range of user postures, offering a smooth vertical adjustment from 600 mm to 1300 mm using a screw-based telescopic mechanism. Each leg consists of three key components: an internal screw shaft, an external screw with a small nut, and a square beam housing a larger nut, all working together to ensure stable and precise motion. Two DC motors independently drive the legs, requiring careful synchronization to maintain level alignment during movement. The system includes a preset height memory feature for user convenience, and the substantial adjustment range accommodates diverse ergonomic needs. Supporting components such as motor mounts, control circuitry, and structural reinforcements complete the design, making it both functional and adaptable for modern workspaces.

projects.title: Automated Quiz Buzzer System
projects.subtitle: Arduino-Based Buzzer System for Competitive Quiz Events Supporting up to 8 Teams
projects.description: This project centers on the design and deployment of an automated quiz buzzer system tailored for competitive quiz events involving up to eight teams. The system integrates a custom-manufactured PCB that consolidates signal routing, input handling, and relay control for indicator lights. After initial prototyping...
projects.longDescription: This project centers on the design and deployment of an automated quiz buzzer system tailored for competitive quiz events involving up to eight teams. The system integrates a custom-manufactured PCB that consolidates signal routing, input handling, and relay control for indicator lights. After initial prototyping, the finalized board supports reliable team input detection and visual feedback through relay-switched outputs. The buzzer logic is built to ensure lockout functionality, preventing simultaneous responses and preserving fairness during high-speed rounds. The system architecture emphasizes modularity and maintainability, with clearly defined input channels and output control paths. The use of relays enables safe switching of external indicators, while the PCB layout minimizes noise and cross-talk between channels. Designed for real-time responsiveness, the system supports rapid identification of the first responder and immediate visual signaling. Its compact footprint and robust signal isolation make it suitable for deployment in academic, corporate, or televised quiz formats. The project demonstrates practical integration of embedded control, digital logic, and hardware interfacing. Overall, it serves as a scalable foundation for future enhancements such as wireless input modules or score-tracking integration.
